test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 28 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a function of mesosomes?

options.text: Increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content
DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells

solution:
The correct answer is __**Locomotion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mesosomes** are invaginations or inward foldings of the plasma membrane in prokaryotic cells, primarily observed in bacteria.
 
• The primary functions of mesosomes include **increasing the surface area of the plasma membrane** for enzymatic activity and facilitating cellular processes such as respiration.
 
• Mesosomes play a crucial role in **DNA replication** and ensuring proper distribution of DNA to daughter cells during cell division.
 
• They also assist in the formation of the cell wall during bacterial cell division.
 
• **Locomotion** is not a function of mesosomes, as bacterial locomotion is mediated by structures like flagella, not mesosomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mesosomes in Prokaryotes:**

 
 
• Mesosomes are more prominent in gram-positive bacteria and are less commonly observed in gram-negative bacteria.
 
• They are thought to play a role in the compartmentalization of metabolic activities within the bacterial cell.
 
 
 
• **Cellular Respiration in Bacteria:**
 
 
• In prokaryotic cells, the plasma membrane, including mesosomes, contains enzymes necessary for cellular respiration and ATP synthesis.
 
• Unlike eukaryotes, bacteria lack mitochondria, so mesosomes help compensate by increasing membrane surface area for these processes.
 
 
 
• **Structures Involved in Locomotion:**
 
 
• Bacterial locomotion is facilitated by the **flagella**, which are long, whip-like structures made of the protein flagellin.
 
• Other structures like pili or fimbriae are involved in adhesion but not in locomotion.
 
 
 
• **Bacterial Cell Division:**
 
 
• Mesosomes are believed to be associated with the segregation of replicated DNA and the formation of the septum during binary fission in bacterial cells.
 
• They play a structural and organizational role during the process of cytokinesis.
